project.name: Elcho

properties.sourceDataset: HES Elcho Castle coordinate and deliberately tight visitor study area

project.boundarySource: The guide uses the current Historic Environment Scotland Elcho Castle location as the locality anchor. This compact editorial visitor-study area is not a parish, estate or legal boundary and excludes Rhynd village and unrelated Tay-side places.
project.researchNotes: Completed current visitor, designation, facilities, dog-policy and trail-screening pass on 2026-09-03. Elcho is represented as the castle-focused locality: Rhynd parish, nearby farm businesses and Tay paths are not transferred into this guide. No independent daytime food provider or named, source-backed in-boundary trail was found in this pass.

touristAppeal.label: Notable Stop
touristAppeal.summary: Elcho is a worthwhile short historic stop because of the exceptionally well-preserved, managed 16th-century castle. Its single principal attraction and lack of a verified separate trail or food offer keep it below a full destination score.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Elcho Castle does not admit pet dogs; assistance dogs are the stated exception. The outdoor approach remains subject to responsible access and the castle should not be chosen as a dog-focused outing.

townGuide.characterTag: Tay-side castle locality in Rhynd parish
townGuide.headline: A carefully preserved 16th-century tower-house
townGuide.intro: Elcho is best approached as a focused heritage visit to Elcho Castle, not as a village amenity centre. Historic Environment Scotland manages the site and publishes the practical arrangements.
perfectFor: Visitors already travelling through the Carse of Gowrie

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Visit Elcho Castle
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Allow around 60–90 minutes for the furnished tower-house and its immediate grounds; use the castle’s visitor-only parking rather than farm or residential access.

townGuide.visitorMood: A contained, managed castle visit rather than a broad settlement trail.

townStudyArea.sourceName: Historic Environment Scotland Elcho Castle designation and visitor location
townStudyArea.notes: A transparent castle-focused study area, deliberately not presented as a settlement, parish or estate boundary.

visitorHighlights.name: Elcho Castle
visitorHighlights.reason: A nationally important, exceptionally well-preserved 16th-century tower-house with a substantial managed interior visit, surviving enclosure remains and clear official visitor information.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: 1 April–30 September: Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 10am–4.30pm; closed Wednesday and Thursday. Closed 1 October–31 March.
visitorHighlights.admission: Adult £8.50; concession £6.80; child £5; Historic Scotland members free (prices published for the 2026 season).

attractionGuide.headline: Elcho Castle
attractionGuide.intro: A managed historic tower-house in Rhynd parish, with a substantial interior visit and immediate grounds.
attractionGuide.parking: Limited, level loose-gravel parking is provided for castle visitors only; do not use farm or residential parking.
attractionGuide.toilets: Toilets are available at the castle visitor facilities.
attractionGuide.picnic: Picnic provision is available at the site.
attractionGuide.foodNote: No separately assessed on-site food offer is published in this guide.

thingsToDo.name: Explore the tower-house
thingsToDo.summary: See the exceptionally well-preserved 16th-century building and its historic rooms.

thingsToDo.name: Read the castle setting
thingsToDo.summary: The scheduled monument includes enclosure remains and associated archaeological evidence around the castle.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Elcho Castle has a deep, distinctive and well-presented managed heritage experience. Its restricted seasonal calendar, limited approach and single-attraction locality constrain journey-worth and access scores.
